card.title: Nintendo Switch power, charge, and HDMI diagnostics guide

claims.statement: A faulty M92T36 IC causes both charging problems and failure to display HDMI video out.
claims.evidence: M92T36 negotiates USB-C power delivery and HDMI alternate mode routing.
claims.quote: M92T36 chip is responsible for negotiating power through the USB-C port, which happens to also be the port through which HDMI out video passes through.

claims.statement: Pin 5 (input) and Pin 6 (output) on M92T36 should read between 3V and 6V DC when power is initiated.
claims.evidence: 0V on Pin 6 indicates a dead M92T36 chip, while 0V on Pin 5 indicates an upstream line short.
claims.quote: In that pin you are supposed to have 3v to 6v. If you have 0v or less, you have a short on that line... 0v in pin 6 means M92T36 is bad.

claims.statement: Replacing temperature setting resistors on BQ24193 with incorrect values prevents battery charging.
claims.evidence: The 3.8k and 5.6k ohm resistors set the battery temperature range for BQ24193 charging logic.
claims.quote: For example if you replace the 5.6kohm resistor with 10k ,bq 24193 will not charge the battery because the temp set for charghing will bee out of range.

claims.statement: Shorted capacitors directly behind the CPU on the back of the PCB indicate an unrepairable board failure.
claims.evidence: Capacitors on the reverse side of the CPU power rail show short to ground when CPU is dead.
claims.quote: There is an area full of capacitor, right behind the CPU, if one of those capacitors is shorted, the switch is trashed.

procedure: Check the USB C input fuse for continuity with multimeter.
Measure battery voltage at connector before and after 30 minutes on charger to confirm BQ24193 charge function.
Disconnect battery and accessories (except eMMC) and check all board capacitors and M92T36 pins for shorts to ground.
Connect battery, press power button, and measure DC voltage at M92T36 Pin 5 and Pin 6 (expect 3V to 6V).
Visually inspect display flex cables and motherboard FPC connectors.
If no display but console powers on, enter RCM mode and inject Hekate payload to test hardware versus firmware corruption.
Check PI3USB30532 chip, surrounding ferrite filters, 0201 caps, and filters if docked HDMI output fails.

cautions: Do not remove the eMMC chip during initial diagnostic checks as it is difficult to reinstall.
Ensure temperature setting resistors near BQ24193 match original exact values (3.8k and 5.6k) or charging will fail.
Avoid excessive heating of the motherboard during USB-C port replacement to prevent PCB blistering.
card.caveats: The text contains compiled forum notes and informal diagnostic tips; resistor measurements must be taken out of circuit for accurate resistance values.
